newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer, seeking direction.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer, seeking direction.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened a bit firmer in thin dealings on Friday as market players awaited some news to provide direction, traders said.
"It has a slightly firmer tone," said one trader. "People are not going to be negative ahead of the weekend."

"There's nothing much going on," another trader said. "We're looking for something to go on." No economic news is expected on Friday from North America except for May's U.S. budget deficit at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded to yield 2.85 percent from 2.86 percent at Thursday's close.
Investors will be watching the Canadian dollar and announcements from the Summit of Eight, the world's most prosperous nations, the second trader said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill strengthened to yield 3.15 percent from 3.18 percent. The one-year T-bill traded unchanged to yield 3.63 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 2.95-3.0 percent, in the middle of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
